questions.question: (R365)'s N5 says no folder name of the host in a bank (data/b755_ferry.txt :54), and (2)(iii) repairs the mirror's folder in the closing alone (data/b755_ferry.txt :11). The data volume's folder that holds PLACE-papers and the mirror stood in 51 of b754's banks, written there by the tools' own captures of PLACE-papers' path: 25 suite run files, 6 suite banks, 4 mirror banks, 2 push-outs, the command capture and 12 others, the act root among them. b755's committed carry bank data/b755_carry_worklist.txt already holds it three times. How far does N5's folder clause reach at this act?

options.label: The mirror's folder; the rest named (Recommended)
options.description: v1.34.6 names the mirror's folder by role in the mirror bank, its json and the closing, as (2)(iii) orders, and no hand-written bank of the seat's names a host folder. The captures that print PLACE-papers' path (the suite's run files and banks, the push-outs, the command capture, the act root) stand as their tools write them; the closing names each kind as outside the clause's reach, the carry bank as committed. Cost: N5's folder clause read at the mirror and the seat's own banks alone; read over every bank by its words, N5 scores REFUTED.

options.label: Every bank from here
options.description: One standing change names PLACE-papers' path and the mirror's folder by role in every capture the act writes from here, a second change beyond (2)(iii)'s one and beyond (2)'s three repairs. The carry bank committed at step zero keeps the folder, so N5 still scores REFUTED on it unless you strike the clause for the banks written before this answer. Cost: the largest change, priced by the seat at 1.5 to 3 h against the ceiling.

options.label: Stop for a ruling
options.description: The seat writes nothing more of Component 1 until you rule on N5's folder clause; step zero stands committed, nothing pushed.
